title: How do we find these eight sums and take aways with a lift?
description: Eight expressions are worked out by drawing or imagining a lift: a sum starts at the first level and moves, a take away starts at the second level and aims for the first. Pairs of expressions give the same answer. Keeko's doubt is that taking away a negative number takes the lift lower.
teaching_notes: One idea: for a take away, the first number is the target level and the second is the starting level, and taking away a negative number gives the same as adding the matching positive number. Watch for students who say a take away must give a smaller number.

source: Try evaluating the expressions by similarly drawing or imagi
video_script.why: The child evaluates sums and take aways of larger integers by drawing a suitable lift.
video_script.substitution: The eight expressions of the book question, solved in four steps with a lift drawn for each.
video_script.anchor: a lift drawn for each expression, with level zero as the ground
video_script.wrong_move: treats taking away negative fifty five as taking away fifty five, so the lift goes lower
video_script.payoff_line: Taking away a negative number gives the same as adding the matching positive number.

final_answer.spoken: negative one hundred fifty five, positive one hundred sixty twice, positive two hundred thirty twice, positive one hundred one twice and positive three thousand

maths_rules: sum x + y: start at x, move y; take away x - y: target x, start y, the answer is the movement
slip: 105 - 55 = 50, and (-55) + 50 = -5, far below the target 105
video_script.design: One lift drawing per step; the pairs that give the same answer are shown side by side.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; eight expressions in two columns; a lift at level -55 with level +105 above it

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about eight expressions.
<bookmark mark='lift'/>The book asks us to draw or imagine a suitable lift for each one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>A lift starts at level negative fifty five and must reach level positive one hundred five. Does it go up or down?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: x + y: start at x, move y;  x - y: target x, start y, the answer is the movement

marks.add: the line x + y: start at x, move y is written
marks.sub: the line x - y: target x, start y is written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>For a sum, the lift starts at the first level and moves by the second number.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>For a take away, the first level is the target, and the second level is the start.

marks.given: the eight expressions are written in two columns

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eight expressions made with plus and with take away.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each expression

marks.find: the words value of each are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the value of each expression.

beats.on_screen: -125 + (-30): start at -125, move 30 further down; 125 + 30 = 155, so -155
narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, negative one hundred twenty five plus negative thirty.
<bookmark mark='amove'/>The lift starts one hundred twenty five below the ground and goes thirty further down.
<bookmark mark='ares'/>The depths add up, so the level is negative one hundred fifty five.

marks.bmove: the lift climbs 55 to the ground and then 105 more, and +160 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step two, positive one hundred five take away negative fifty five.
The lift starts fifty five below the ground and must reach level one hundred five.
<bookmark mark='bmove'/>It climbs fifty five to the ground, then one hundred five more, so one hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Positive one hundred five plus positive fifty five also gives one hundred sixty.

marks.dmove: the lift climbs 150 to the ground and then 80 more, and +230 is written
marks.h: +1500 - (-1500) is written and the lift climbs 1500 twice, giving +3000

narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>Step three, positive eighty take away negative one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='dmove'/>The lift climbs one hundred fifty to the ground, then eighty more, so two hundred thirty.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Positive eighty plus positive one hundred fifty also gives two hundred thirty.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Positive one thousand five hundred take away negative one thousand five hundred. The lift climbs that distance twice, so three thousand.

marks.fmove: the lift climbs from level -200 up to level -99, and +101 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='f'/>Step four, negative ninety nine take away negative two hundred.
<bookmark mark='fmove'/>It climbs two hundred to the ground, then comes down ninety nine. The movement is positive one hundred one.
<bookmark mark='g'/>Negative ninety nine plus positive two hundred also gives one hundred one.

marks.pay: the pairs of expressions with equal answers are joined by a bracket
marks.first: the first three answers are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Taking away a negative number gives the same as adding the matching positive number.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first three are negative one hundred fifty five, positive one hundred sixty, and positive one hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The next two are both positive two hundred thirty. The next two are both positive one hundred one. The last is positive three thousand.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 50 crossed out; the lift pressed 50 from level -55 stops at level -5, far below level +105

marks.short: the lift pressed 50 from level -55 stops at level -5
marks.fix: 50 is struck out and the gap up to level +105 lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is fifty, because taking away takes the lift lower.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Press fifty from level negative fifty five, and the lift stops at level negative five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>That is still below the ground. Taking away a negative number adds, so the answer is one hundred sixty.
